newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Germany's DG Bank to buy 55.98 pct of Takarekbank. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Germany's DG Bank to buy 55.98 pct of Takarekbank. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects to replace earlier story. Hungarian state privatisation agency APV has corrected most figures.)
Germany's Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank won a tender for the privatisation of the 55.98 percent of Hungary's Takarekbank Rt, Takarekbank officials told a news conference on Wednesday.
Takarekbank is the umbrella bank of Hungarian savings cooperatives which have more than 1,600 branches and some two million retail customers.

"With the privatisation a new era will begin for the savings cooperative sector," said Takarekbank's CEO Zsolt Hernadi, adding that he expects the investor to accelerate the modernisation of the savings cooperatives.
Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt is selling an altogether 60/98 percent stake in the bank, which has a registered capital of 1.34 billion forints.
The purchase price for the whole 60.98 percent stake on offer was 41.3 million German marks.
The price of the privatised stake is 531 percent of the face value of the shares, Hernadi said, adding that this was the highest price per share ever in Hungarian bank privatisation.

Five percent within the 60.98 percent stake will bought by the insurance company Hungaria Biztosito Rt, which submitted a joint bid with DG Bank. Hungaria is the Hungarian subsidiary of Allianz. The other bidder was GiroCredit of Austria.
